what_it_does: Image sensors capture enormous amounts of pixel data, most of which gets thrown away after compression for downstream AI tasks. Instead, this work embeds lightweight compression inside the sensor itself: a tiny 1-bit encoder built into the photodiode array that directly outputs task-relevant features (e.g., edges, corners) instead of raw pixels. The encoder is co-designed with the AI model it feeds—they're optimized together. This cuts data transmission and energy consumption dramatically by extracting only what matters for the task at the source.
